about.title: About Body Fat Calculator
about.description: The Body Fat Calculator estimates your body fat percentage using various measurement methods including waist circumference, hip measurements, and other body dimensions. Body fat percentage is a more accurate indicator of health than BMI alone. Understanding your body composition helps in setting realistic fitness goals and tracking progress more effectively than weight alone.

faq.q: What's a healthy body fat percentage for men and women?
faq.a: For men: 10-20% is considered healthy, with essential fat at 2-5%. For women: 16-25% is healthy, with essential fat at 10-13%. Athletes may have lower percentages. Our body fat calculator provides detailed category classifications for accurate assessment.

faq.q: How accurate are body fat calculator estimates?
faq.a: Body fat calculators provide estimates with a 3-5% margin of error when measurements are taken correctly. For more precise measurements, consider DEXA scans or professional body composition analysis. Our calculator uses proven formulas for reliable home estimates.

faq.q: Which body fat measurement method is most accurate?
faq.a: The Navy method (waist and neck for men, waist, neck, and hips for women) is generally considered most accurate for home measurements. Our calculator offers multiple methods so you can compare results and choose your preferred approach.

faq.q: How often should I measure my body fat percentage?
faq.a: Monthly body fat measurements are sufficient for tracking progress and avoiding daily fluctuations due to hydration, food intake, and other factors. Consistent measurement timing and conditions improve accuracy.

faq.q: Is body fat percentage more important than BMI?
faq.a: Body fat percentage provides more detailed information about body composition than BMI alone. It distinguishes between muscle and fat mass, making it especially valuable for athletes and fitness enthusiasts. Use both metrics together for comprehensive health assessment.

faq.q: How do I take accurate body measurements for the calculator?
faq.a: Use a flexible measuring tape on bare skin when possible. Measure waist at the narrowest point, hips at the widest point, and neck just below the Adam's apple. Take measurements at the same time of day for consistency.
